phases.message: Human approved this phase; continuing after it.

phases.remediation_plan: Phase 1: Extract each fragment into self-contained module with explicit exports. Phase 2: Implement build-order validation. Phase 3: Migrate jsdom to devDependencies. Phase 4: Add runtime tests. Phase 5: Incrementally refactor while preserving offline-first constraints.
findings: HIGH | Tight coupling via global PS.* namespace across 142 source fragments (manifest.txt) - fragment execution order is critical and any reordering breaks functionality
MEDIUM | No module encapsulation - all fragments share single script scope PS.* with no encapsulation, making dependency management fragile (build.mjs)
MEDIUM | jsdom listed in package.json dependencies despite project claiming 'zero dependencies' for runtime - potential build-time dependency leak (package.json)
LOW | Syntax validation only via node --check in build.mjs, no runtime behavior validation, risk of undetected logical errors
INFO | Single-file HTML output (ProcureSherpa-v2.0.html) satisfies offline-first requirement but limits modularity and maintainability
